rules.statement: Make any OpenID Connect mechanism that depends on third-party cookies in iframes (Front-Channel Logout, Session Management) available but disabled by default, so it turns on only through an opt-in server setting whose default is false.
rules.why: Browsers are removing third-party cookies, so these mechanisms are unreliable by design. A stock OP must not depend on them, advertise them, or set a non-HttpOnly browser-state cookie.
rules.check: Look for new or changed settings for frontchannel_logout_supported, frontchannel_logout_session_supported, session_management_supported or similar iframe/cookie-based features whose default is true, or code paths that run the mechanism without checking the opt-in setting.

rules.statement: Keep what the OP actually does in line with what discovery advertises: emit protocol parameters and behaviors only while the matching advertised capability setting is enabled.
rules.why: Relying parties decide what to rely on from discovery metadata, so behavior that does not match the advertisement breaks the contract.
rules.check: Look for code that appends iss/sid to front-channel logout URIs, emits session_state, or exposes check_session_iframe without first checking the matching server capability setting.

rules.statement: Reject client registrations or settings that need a server capability that is disabled, for example a frontchannel_logout_uri while front-channel logout is unsupported, or frontchannel_logout_session_required while session support is off.
rules.why: This validation keeps per-client configuration consistent with the server's advertised capabilities, so what the OP does always matches what it advertises.
rules.check: Look for new per-client capability settings that are added without a validation rule rejecting them when the server-level capability is disabled.

rules.statement: Treat Front-Channel Logout as a best-effort addition to Back-Channel Logout, never a replacement: back-channel logout must stay always on and must not depend on the front-channel setting.
rules.why: Back-Channel Logout is the preferred mechanism that works without cookies. Front-channel logout is fragile by design and is only a supplement.
rules.check: Look for changes that skip, disable or condition back-channel logout delivery on front-channel logout being enabled, or that route logout only through the front-channel iframes.

rules.statement: Delete the OP browser-state cookie used for Session Management on logout, and issue it with SameSite=None and Secure (non-HttpOnly only because the check-session iframe script has to read it).
rules.why: The browser state drives session_state change detection, so it must be cleared when the session ends. It is framed cross-site, so it needs SameSite=None; Secure.
rules.check: Look for a browser-state cookie set without SameSite=None/Secure, or logout paths that don't delete it.

rules.statement: Compute the OIDC session_state value as a salted SHA-256 digest of the client id, the origin of the client's redirect URI, and the opaque OP browser state, following Session Management 1.0.
rules.why: The check-session iframe script recomputes the same value to answer the RP's postMessage poll with changed/unchanged, so both sides must use the same inputs.
rules.check: Look for session_state computations that leave out the salt, use a different hash, or use an origin other than the one from the client's redirect_uri.
